To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the H2 flow duration prior to growth has a significant impact on the growth of graphene on Cu substrate.
the growth of monolayer graphene on Cu is favored when the H2 flow interval is kept to the minimum (5 min).
the growth of single layer graphene on copper is favored when H2 flow interval prior to growth is 5 min and growth temperature 1000 °C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hydrogen and its duration of utilization for the production of high quality graphene by chemical vapor deposition.
the role of H2 flow duration and the effect of H2 on the surface chemistry of copper, which can be used to grow monolayer graphene.
a method of growth of graphene on Cu foil by LPCVD, where a minimum flow of H2 is used for growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
H2 treatment for longer time intervals (more than 5 min) is not desirable as it leads to secondary nucleation sites.
the H2 treatment of the Cu substrate for a minimum time of 5 min is required for monolayer graphene growth and the H2 flow duration should be kept as short as possible for safety reasons.
H2 treatment for 35 min prior to growth favors multilayer graphene growth, whereas 5 min H2 flow favors the growth of monolayer graphene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a flow interval of 10 min of H2 gas is optimum for the growth of large crystalline monolayer graphene.
the growth mechanism is dependent on the H2 treatment time interval.
H2 flow interval plays a key role for the growth of graphene on copper surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
H2 treatment prior to growth is essential for the growth of graphene, and it can be used as a parameter for the growth of monolayer graphene.
the H2 flow rate can be reduced to 10 sccm for the growth of graphene without compromising the growth of monolayer graphene.
the H2 flow duration can be used for controlling the nucleation density and growth of graphene.
